To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

different growth factors act directly or indirectly on dopaminergic neurons in midbrain cultures, that these growth factors act on different subsets of dopaminergic cells and, thus, may play a role in establishing the functional and morphological diversity of these neurons.

different dopaminergic neurons respond to growth factors with distinct patterns of gene expression, that growth factors affect midbrain dopaminergie neurons by indirect mechanisms that require cell-cell communication, and that growth factors might contribute to the morphological and physiological heterogeneity of dopaminergic midbrain neurons.

growth factors induce c-fos expression directly in different populations of dopaminergic cells and indirectly in dopaminergic neurons via a glia-mediated glutamate activation of N-metlyl-D-aspartate-receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which extracellular growth factors regulate the survival, differentiation and functional maturation of midbrain dopaaminergic neurons.
the molecular mechanisms of growth factor-induced gene regulation in dopaminergic neurons and their role in dopaminergic neuron development and plasticity.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the survival and differentiation processes of midbrain dopamine neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
growth factors act in a cell-specific manner and that their effects are modulated by cell-cell communication.
different growth factors induce Fos expression in different subpopulations of dopaminergic cells.
growth factors affect the survival and/or differentiation of midbrain dopamingeric neurons through a complex interplay of direct and indirect mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
growth factors affect different subsets of dopaminergic midbrain neurons by different mechanisms.
growth factor signalling is involved in establishing the functional diversity of mesencephalically derived dopamine neurons.
growth factors are considered pivotal in the development, maintenance and function of mesencaphalic dopaminergic neurones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
growth factors are not only important for the maintenance and function of dopaminergic cells but also play an important role in the development of the midbrain dopaminergenic system.
growth factors are involved in the development and function of dopaminergic systems in the brain.
the same growth factor can have different effects in different neurons, depending on the cell type and the cell environment.
